snippet.title: A Billion Software Engineers: Paul Biggar, CTO @ Dark
snippet.description:
Paul Biggar has co-founded Dark the tools company for software engineering primitives.

Previously, he founded CircleCI–the popular continuous integration service–and obtained his PhD in Computer Science from Trinity University in Dublin, Ireland.

In this episode we cover:

- the scope of engineering tools that Dark aims to provide,
- the chronology of Paul’s career story so far, from academics to startups,
- the first software Paul ever wrote

For more: https://theaccidentalengineer.com/billion-software-engineers-paul-biggar-cto-dark/

snippet.title: To the States: George Arison, Co-Founder @ Shift
snippet.description:
George Arison co-founded Shift out of his apartment in the Castro neighorhood of San Francisco.

Starting with CraigList ads, the company has grown to be a national brand for buying & selling used cars.

Hear George’s story, starting from a childhood in the USSR, immigrating to the USA, and becoming an entrepreneur.

snippet.title: Why software apprenticeships?
snippet.description:
With Meggie Mahnken, Senior Director of Education @ Hackbright Academy:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/bootcamp-curriculum-meggie-mahnken-hackbright-academy-interview/

snippet.title: Customer Education Management: Sumeru Chatterjee, Gong.io
snippet.description:
Sumeru Chatterjee created the international community CustomerEducation.org.

Besides leading the conversation about “customer education” teams in tech companies, Sumo is joining Gong.io and previously worked at Addepar.

In this appearance we cover:

- what “customer education” means
- where these teams originate within companies
- which parts of the business lifecycle are touched by customer educators

For the full episode: https://theaccidentalengineer.com/customer-education-management-sumo-chatterjee-gong-io/

snippet.title: PM Storytellers: Ryan Harper, SVP Product @ Citi Ventures
snippet.description:
Ryan Harper of Citi Ventures joins to share his path into product management.

Previously, he has been a product manager at Conde Naste, WebMD and IHeartMedia.

In this appearance we cover:

- the trials & tribulations of working on software products
- the data & methods that product managers use to identify the “voice of the customer”
- the importance of sharing a story with data and not just data

For the full interview:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/product-manager-storytelling-ryan-harper-svp-product-citi-ventures/

snippet.title: Bootcamp Curriculum: Meggie Mahnken, Hackbright Academy
snippet.description:
Meggie Mahnken joins the show to share about Hackbright Academy, the all-women software engineering bootcamp.

We also heard from Meggie about her own story of getting into software engineering from an undergraduate degree from UC Berkeley in Gender Studies.

In this appearance we cover:

- what Hackbright curriculum looks like
- which job titles Hackbright alumnae have tended to get out of the program
- how Hackbright admissions interviews are like real job interviews

For the full interview:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/bootcamp-curriculum-meggie-mahnken-hackbright-academy-interview/

snippet.title: Rapidly Building Software: Anand Kulkarni, CEO @ Crowdbotics
snippet.description:
Anand Kulkarni re-joins the show to share the latest with Crowdbotics, the software building service.

Anand appeared on the show in Season 1 last year.

In this appearance we discussed:

- what can be learned from scanning open source package indices (PyPI, RubyGems, NPM)
- how to choose technologies as an early stage startup
- when you should trust 3rd party platforms for building developer products

For the full interview: https://theaccidentalengineer.com/building-software-rapido-anand-kulkarni-crowdbotics/

snippet.title: Continuous Integration Today: Ray Sennewald, Senior Software Engineer @ Box, Inc
snippet.description:
Ray Sennewald manages build and release pipelines at Box, the file-hosting corporation.

In this episode we discuss:

the trials & tribulations of building software for many different devices
how a startup might do continuous integration vs. a public company
what best practices exist for managing your multi-platform software builds

For the full episode: https://theaccidentalengineer.com/continuous-integration-ray-sennewald-engineer-box/

snippet.title: Consulting on Growth Marketing: Will Leiter, Advisor
snippet.description:
Will Leiter consults to tech companies at his own Will Leiter Consulting.

He’d previously served as Head of Pro Growth at Thumbtack, the local services startup valued at over $1 billion.

In this episode we discuss:

- what growth marketing means at tech companies
- how brand & performance marketing are different
- what role software plays in the consulting that Will performs for his clients

For the full interview visit our website: https://theaccidentalengineer.com/consulting-growth-marketing-software-will-leiter/

snippet.title: Designing Services: Andrea Fineman, Getaround
snippet.description:
Andrea designs the way that users interact with the Getaround car rental service.

She came to Getaround by way of Adaptive Path (now Capitale One) and received her Masters from Carnegie Mellon University.

In this episode we discuss:

- what is service design
- how product management and service design are distinguished
- the Google projects Minnie was involved with in her tenure there

For the full interview:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/designing-services-andrea-fineman-getaround/

snippet.title: Operators & Startups: Minnie Ingersoll, Investor @ 10110 Ventures
snippet.description:
Minnie Ingersoll recently joined 10110 Ventures as an investor in tech startups.

Before becoming an investor Minnie co-founded Shift.com and served as COO for 5 years. Originally studying computer science in undergrad, Minnie also spent over 10 years at Google as a PM.

In this episode we discuss:

- the responsibilities of a COO within a startup
- unique qualities of Los Angeles-based startup environment
- the variety of Google projects Minnie got involved with in her long tenure there

For the full interview:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/operators-startups-minnie-ingersoll-investor-10110-ventures/

snippet.title: Skills Tests & Compensation: Aline Lerner, CEO @ Interviewing.io
snippet.description:
Aline Lerner, CEO + Founder at Interviewing.io rejoins the show to share engineering career insights.

We cover lots of job market data in this episode including:

- the relationship between job interview performance and compensation
- advice to employers on how to proctor technical interviews
- favorite snacks to be eaten during interviews(!)

Original interview:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/skills-tests-and-compensation-aline-lerner-interviewing-io/

snippet.title: Operative Sales: Taft Love, Vice President of Revenue @ HouseCanary
snippet.description:
Taft Love runs inside sales at HouseCanary, a home-valuation startup that offers Software-as-a-Service.

We discuss how software engineers and sales employees communicate in order to inform the direction a company builds its products.

snippet.title: Job Search Criteria: Chang She, Engineering Manager @ Cloudera
snippet.description:
Chang She started his career at hedge fund AQR Capital Management before leaving finance to co-found DataPad with his college classmate, Wes McKinney.

DataPad was acquired by Cloudera in 2014 and now Chang manages a team within Cloudera.

We discuss how contributing to open source software has impacted Chang’s career, and the 3 criteria that Chang recommends you evaluate before accepting a job offer.

For more info about Chang and the interview: 

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/job-search-criteria-chang-she-cloudera/

snippet.title: Technical Interviewing Anonymous: Aline Lerner, CEO @ Interviewing.io
snippet.description:
Aline Lerner, CEO of Interviewing.io, has been on every side of the software engineering hiring equation.

She started her career as a software engineer out of MIT, took on recruiting, started her own recruiting agency, and now has formulated a test environment for job candidates to prepare their job interviewing skills.

If you’re curious about how you can get *better* at interviewing for software engineering jobs, then listen to our conversation to find the answers!

For the full text transcript see the interview on the Accidental Engineer:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/technical-interviewing-anonymous-aline-lerner-ceo-interviewing-io/

snippet.title: Returning for Computer Science: Carol Toro
Co-founding a Hardware Startup: Aaron Zarraga, CTO of Sensel
snippet.description:
Aaron Zarraga began his career as a hardware engineer at Amazon in San Jose on the Concept Engineer team.

Leaving his full-time job with Amazon to co-found a hardware startup (Sensel) was a difficult decision with lots of learning moments for Aaron.

We cover Aaron’s professional background, and Aaron shares hard-earned advice for engineers interested in the development process of hardware products:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/prototype-to-product-aaron-zarraga-cto-sensel/

snippet.title: Accounting to Coding: Kat Gordiienko, Senior Analytics Engineer @ Netflix
snippet.description:
Kat Gordiienko began her career working full-time as an accountant while completing her senior year of college as an economics major.

Short on time between her job and education Kat was forced to adopt programming on the job. She taught herself SQL and—after a number of subsequent years in BI consulting–ultimately took a Senior Analytics Engineer role with Netflix.

This interview covers Kat’s background and advice she has for accidental engineers like she once was herself. 

To view the interview on the Accidental Engineer site:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/accounting-to-coding-kat-gordiienko-interview-netflix/

snippet.title: How to Start Your Career in CS: Tom Alcorn
snippet.description:
Tom Alcorn of Flux.io joins us for a conversation about how he flipped a major in Math & Physics into a software engineering career.

Topics of this episode include:

- why Tom’s got a fascination with programming languages and LLVM
- what are the educational resources Tom has used to educate himself on CS
- how Tom’s time at MIT led to his first data science job and how his first job led to a software engineering role

For the full text transcript see our website at TheAccidentalEngineer.com:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/programming-languages-for-newbs-tom-alcorn-flux/

snippet.title: Machine Learning at Netflix: Jose Moreno
snippet.description:
Jose Moreno, Senior Software Architect at Netflix joined us for a conversation about his post-college career so far.

Topics of this episode include:

- how Jose ended up at Netflix, working on machine learning problems in the Content Algorithms team
- what were some of Jose’s formative computer science experiences and his advice for current students
- who was Jose’s favorite professor at Harvey Mudd College, his alma mater

For the full text transcript see our site at theaccidentalengineer.com:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/machine-learning-netflix-jose-moreno/

snippet.title: Failure Analysis + Testing in Software Engineering: Andrew Schriner
snippet.description:
Andrew, Principal Software Engineer at LeadGenius, shares with us how to evaluate, estimate and control for the risk of failure in software engineering businesses.

Topics include:

- what is "FEMA" analysis
- where risk originates from in building software
- how to leverage a non-CS PhD into a career in software engineering

For a full text transcript visit our website at the Accidental Engineer:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/testing-for-software-failure-andy-schriner/

snippet.title: Evaluating Equity Offers: Ruby Bhattacharya of Coinbase
snippet.description:
Ruby re-joins us to give some insight from the employer side of the table about how job candidates should evaluate the equity component of a job offer.

Topics include:

- what's a 409A valuation
- what's a strike price
- why you should tread carefully in asking for information about early stage company's finances

For a full text transcript visit the Accidental Engineer website at:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/evaluating-equity-in-job-offers-ruby-bhattacharya-coinbase/

snippet.title: PhD to Data Scientist: Jeremy Karp of Lyft
snippet.description:
Wondering what the job market looks like after a PhD program? What it takes to get a data scientist role coming from academia?

Our close friend Jeremy Karp just obtained his PhD and will soon start a new role as a Data Scientist at Lyft.

Topics of our conversation include:

- what pros and cons Jeremy weighed in considering a PhD program
- how Jeremy prepared for his most recent job interviews
- which interview formats and questions are top Data Scientist employers utilizing to evaluate candidates

For a full text transcript of the interview visit the Accidental Engineer website:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/phd-to-data-scientist-lyft-career-jeremy-karp/

snippet.title: Product Designer Things: Steven Striegel
snippet.description:
Steven Striegel is sole product designer at San Francisco-based Mux, a video analytics platform with clients like PBS and Funny or Die.

We had Steven on to share his career journey so far: from college in Fargo, North Dakota, making the West move to join tech-based startups in the software-as-a-service economy.

Topics include:

- what the “product designer” job title entails
- how to work efficiently with a team of engineers
- which feedback loops Steven endorses for soliciting customer feedback and quickly iterating product designs

For a full text transcript of our conversation visit the Accidental Engineer website at:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/product-design-for-dummies-steven-striegel/

snippet.title: Music & Software Engineering: Christian Foster Howes
snippet.description:
Christian Foster Howes majored in Computer Engineering & Musical Performance as an undergrad at University of Michigan. Fifteen years later and Christian has held VP of Engineering roles at startups as well as founding Little Mission Studio, a private music school in San Francisco.

He joined us for a conversation about the importance of develop your skillset beyond writing lines of code.

Topics include:

- why musical performance prepares you for working on a software engineering team
- what Christian’s evaluation criteria are for evaluating engineering resumés
- how to achieve redundancy in musical performance and software engineering teams

For the full text transcript visit the Accidental Engineer:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/musical-software-engineering-christian-foster-howes/

snippet.title: Marketing Math: Rachael Maltiel Swenson of eBay
snippet.description:
Rachael Maltiel Swenson of eBay joined us as a guest on the show to share some career advice for analytics-minded careerists.

Topics include:

- how Rachael found her way to eBay via Bain Consulting, grad school (!), Expedia and Pinterest
- why you should always learn SQL
- what to know about the hiring manager when applying for that marketing analytics role you're interested in

For a text transcript view the show on our website: the Accidental Engineer

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/marketing-math-rachael-maltiel-swenson-ebay-analytics/

snippet.description:

We cover:

- what were some of the product tradeoffs in Craig's tenure running Heroku's hosted-Postgres offering

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/product-manage-dropbox-pm-ketan-nayak/

Elliot Godzich joins us to share his tale of working for a startup through its acquisition and why he made the decision to leave the salaried life to start a new business in virtual reality software.

Topics include:

- what was Elliot’s background that afforded him to make the entrepeneurial leap (and why he would do it again)
- why you should fail fast
- how much money Elliot lost in the process

For discussion and a text transcript visit our website at the Accidental Engineer:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/shutting-down-vr-startup-elliot-godzich/

snippet.title: Data Science for Health: Alyssa Whitwell of Clover Health

snippet.description:
Charlotte joined us to share her story so far, graduating high school to pursue astrophysics dreams, majoring in math, and then re-orienting her career a few years after undergrad.

We cover topics like:

- what was radically different from her first job out of school to her latest role as an engineer
- which resources Charlotte used to self-teach herself in preparation for his first engineering role
- what "safety rails" employers have in place to help save new employees from causing nightmare scenarios on the job

- the best (and specific) resources to prepare yourself for engineering job interviews
- what leaving Google for a startup and then re-applying is like (!)

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/preparing-tech-interviews-paul-carleton-stripe/

- how 20% of Americans have a criminal record

We had the fortune of sitting down with Alex to hear about why he left Microsoft and how he landed his current role at TuneIn, a San Francisco-based podcast startup.

Covered topics include:

- the VC illuminati that can place you into a job at a startup

snippet.title: What the sh*t is WordPress? Kyle Feeley shares why it was a big deal back in the day
snippet.description:
Kyle rejoins us to share his thoughts and feelings about the past and present of website development with WordPress.

He started his career implementing custom website designs for small and medium-size businesses, picking up HTML, CSS, JavaScript and a little bit of PHP along the way.

Little known facts:

- TechCrunch was and is built using WordPress
- Facebook was and is built using PHP, the same programming language behind WordPress
- Kyle is a consummate baller, shot-caller

To view more detail, visit here:

http://theaccidentalengineer.com/what-the-sht-is-wordpress-kyle-feeley-shares-why-it-was-a-big-deal-back-in-the-day/

snippet.title: The Tech Job Market in Recession with Ruby Bhattacharya of Coinbase
snippet.description:
Ruby joins us again to share some perspective on the historical dips in the job market for software engineers, specifically the dot-com bubble of 1999 and the global financial crisis of 2008.

Some of the topics we cover:

- what jobs in tech bounced back first
- what happened to software engineers through both job market downturns
- how job placement and interviewing for engineers is different in a recession vs. today

What was your experience through those job market downturns?

View this video on our website here:

https://theaccidentalengineer.com/tech-job-market-recessions-ruby-bhattacharya-coinbase/

snippet.title: Ryan Baumbach, Senior iOS Engineer @ Madefire
snippet.description:
Ryan describes his career arc from working in IT to testing and from from testing to engineering.

He shares how he did it: through self-study and zero post-graduate studies, through two recessions and ~8 different iOS versions.

We cover topics including:

– why non-engineering roles can be a great foot in the door
– what are the bare minimum requirements for getting started with iOS development
